answer: Resist Sybils with per-identity proof of work: before an agent can trade, it must solve a fresh computational puzzle bound to its key, cheap for peers to verify but costly in time and electricity to produce. One honest agent pays this once, like crossing a bridge; a farm trying to flood the meadow with thousands of fakes must pay it thousands of times. Unlike a comet that flashes and fades, the cost cannot be reused or copied across identities, so mass forgery costs more than any spam or vote-rigging gain.
